title: Geometry-optimized hyperbolic codes for modular fault-tolerant quantum architectures
summary: Quantum fault tolerance is a prerequisite to harness the full potential of quantum computers. However, achieving fault tolerance remains a major challenge since it requires optimizing tradeoffs between several intertwined theoretical and experimental parameters, including the encoding rate, code distance, parity-check weights, code planarity, and routing. Surface codes remain strong candidates for fault tolerance due to their simple geometric structure, established decoding methods, locality, and experimental attainability.
